key_insight: Higher-gradient regularization enables an existence proof for finite-strain elastoplastic evolution, while vectorized FEM makes logarithmic-strain computations efficient.
engineering_relevance: The framework supports elastoplastic simulations with large rotations and deformations without substantially increasing computational cost.
method: Use logarithmic strains with von Mises plasticity and linear kinematic hardening.
Add higher-gradient regularization and prove existence of energetic solutions under time-dependent Dirichlet loading.
Vectorize MATLAB FEM using page-wise matrix functions and a custom vectorization library.
evidence_signal: Computational benchmarks report significant acceleration of local tensor operations and robust handling of large rotations and deformations.
watch_item: The existence result relies on higher-gradient regularization; it does not establish well-posedness of the unregularized quadratic Hencky model.
paper_title: Mathematical analysis and vectorized FEM implementation of logarithmic strain space framework for finite strains: a case study on elastoplasticity
